clue.text: Orbiting object's business fulfilled

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
to have met a target or demand is to have fulfilled it

explanation.surface: A satellite company boasting that its orbital mission has been accomplished.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy body travelling round the sun on a long elliptical path.

clue.text: Making concessions can be embarrassing

blocks.note: first meaning: settling differences by each side giving way
second meaning: revealing or shaming, as a photo might be

explanation.surface: Giving ground in a negotiation may leave you red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means meeting someone halfway and also exposing someone to scandal or shame, as in a compromising photograph.

clue.text: Spread ruin, vicious in rage

indicators.note: something vicious is wild and violent, so the letters following are thrown about

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone furiously wrecking things everywhere in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Spread looks like a verb but is the noun: something spread on bread. In rage is fodder, not a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute that is spread on toast and bread.

clue.text: Shock shown by artist with uncertain expression amid cheers

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so these letters sit inside the word for thanks

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist
um is the sound of someone hesitating
ta is informal British for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A painter hesitating, stunned, while a crowd applauds.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers here is the British way of saying thanks, not applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is severe emotional shock or a physical injury, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Joker with trick taking in broadcasters?

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a con is a swindle or trick
the media are the broadcasters and the press

explanation.surface: A prankster fooling the television people with a stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that broadcasters stands loosely for the media in general.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is someone who tells jokes for a living, and joker is a common synonym.

clue.text: Miserly type, cold fish occupied by collection

indicators.note: a place occupied by something has it inside, so the pile sits within the other letters

blocks.note: C stands for cold on a tap
a heap is a pile or collection of things
skate is a flat sea fish

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted person described as an unfriendly cold fish holding on to a stash.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold fish suggests an aloof person, but the two words are separate pieces of wordplay, and the collection occupies the gap between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person who hates spending money, the same as a miser.

clue.text: Flightless bird caught finally in ditch

indicators.note: finally means at the very end, picking the closing letter

blocks.note: the moa was a huge flightless bird of New Zealand
last letter of caught

explanation.surface: A bird that cannot fly ends up trapped at the bottom of a trench.
explanation.definitionFit: A moat is a deep water-filled ditch dug round a castle for defence.

clue.text: Decline drink with convert

blocks.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
to turn something is to change or convert it

explanation.surface: Turning down a drink offered by a new religious recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Decline and drink both look like verbs, as in refusing a drink, but decline is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a drop in economic or business activity, a fall or decline.

clue.text: Keen to retain old bypass

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so the outer word keeps a letter within it

blocks.note: avid means eager or keen
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone eager to keep an old road rather than build a new ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: Bypass suggests the noun for a ring road, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to go round it or keep away from it, which is to bypass it.

clue.text: Novelist, ace in treatment of good raw matter

indicators.note: raw material put through treatment is processed and comes out in a new form
one item is placed in among the reworked letters

blocks.note: an ace is the one card in a suit, written A
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer praised for skilfully processing promising raw material into fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The thirteen letters of good raw matter are rearranged and the A slotted in as the second letter to give MARGARET ATWOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Atwood is the Canadian author of The Handmaid's Tale and many other novels.

clue.text: Opera spoilt by grand poses

indicators.note: something spoilt is damaged and no longer in its proper form, so the letters are messed up

blocks.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A performance ruined by singers striking theatrical attitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: By looks like a link word, but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Porgy and Bess is George Gershwin's 1935 opera set in South Carolina.

clue.text: Democrat in range with a quiet plan

indicators.note: the politician sits in the middle of the word for wandering

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for a US Democrat
to range over an area is to roam
taken as written
p, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A US politician out on the campaign trail with a low-key strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside ROAM, then A and P follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A road map is a figurative term for a step-by-step strategy or schedule toward a goal.

clue.text: Projection: one Oscar for production company

blocks.note: a stud is a small knob projecting from a surface
the Roman numeral for one
Oscar is the NATO alphabet word for the letter O

explanation.surface: A film company celebrating a single Academy Award for one of its pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar looks like the film award, which suits the movie-business surface, but it is just the radio code word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Film studios such as Paramount or Warner are the companies that make and release movies.

clue.text: Applauded then dismissed, being of no more use

blocks.note: to clap is to applaud
simply orders the pieces
in cricket a dismissed batsman is out

explanation.surface: A batsman cheered by the crowd then sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: Clapped-out is British slang for worn out, used especially of old cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clapped-out is worn out and broken down from long use, so no longer serviceable.

clue.text: Principal speaker's head of hair

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard, not read, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a mane is a long thick head of hair, as on a horse or lion

explanation.surface: Remarking on the most notable feature of someone's flowing locks.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal and main both mean chief or most important, as in the principal or main reason.

clue.text: Tomfoolery from poet going into air guitar initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it
the writer goes into the middle, held between the other letters

blocks.note: the sky is the air above us
Philip Larkin, the English poet
the first letter of guitar

explanation.surface: A distinguished poet caught miming on an air guitar, which is pure clowning.
explanation.walkthrough: Air guitar looks like one phrase but splits into two separate pieces of wordplay. Philip Larkin was a twentieth-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylarking is boisterous, playful messing about, the same sort of horseplay that tomfoolery describes.

clue.text: One rages about endless ceremony and annoyances

indicators.note: endless means losing the end, so the final letter is dropped
about means around, so the angry word goes round the shortened ritual

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
to rant is to rage loudly
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Somebody ranting about interminable ceremonial and other irritations.
explanation.walkthrough: One looks like part of a phrase about someone raging, but it stands alone as the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritants are things that cause annoyance or irritation, so they are annoyances in a plural noun.

clue.text: Bar, secure, managed without a fearsome guard dog

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the single named letter is removed
managed suggests the letters are handled and arranged differently

blocks.note: the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Locking up and securing the gates, managing without a guard dog.
explanation.walkthrough: One A is removed from bar secure before the rest are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Cerberus is the three-headed hound that guards the gates of the underworld.

clue.text: Potter's eye transformed conventional image

indicators.note: something transformed is changed in form, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Harry Potter's famous look turning into a cliched picture of a wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype is a fixed, oversimplified mental picture of a type of person, widely held.

clue.text: Song in particular I admire

indicators.note: in tells us the solution lies inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the single letter and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Picking out one tune as a personal favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio, a specific kind of song.

clue.text: Published title for monk? Not planned

blocks.note: a newspaper ran a story when it published it
Dom is the honorific given to some Benedictine monks

explanation.surface: A monk's book appears in print under an unexpected title.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means occurring by chance with no plan, method or deliberate choice behind it.

clue.text: Handy tips for novice after bounty

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of novice
first and last letters of after
first and last letters of bounty

explanation.surface: Useful advice for a beginner once the reward has been collected.
explanation.walkthrough: Tips applies to each of the three following words in turn, not just novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handy is close at hand, conveniently located within easy reach.

clue.text: Supply answer about love for perfume

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for love is enclosed

blocks.note: to arm is to supply with weapons
A is the abbreviation for answer
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Providing a reply about love in exchange for some scent.
explanation.walkthrough: Supply is the verb meaning to equip with weapons; the love letter lands inside the joined pieces rather than wrapping them.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant smell or fragrance, which is what a perfume gives off.

clue.text: Former partner stopped missing husband? That's grand

indicators.note: missing means going without, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
halted means stopped
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone's ex no longer turning up, minus the husband, and finding that wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Exalted means lofty or of high rank, the same elevated sense as grand.

clue.text: Ruler in for astonishing upset

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A monarch due for an astonishing overthrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was an emperor of Russia, a supreme ruler with absolute power.

clue.text: Communication between writers in agreement

blocks.note: first meaning: letters exchanged by people writing to each other
second meaning: a close match or similarity between things

explanation.surface: Two authors whose letters show they see eye to eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an exchange of letters and a matching relationship, as in a correspondence between two sets of figures.

clue.text: Second novel in stark language

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters come out in a fresh order

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A second book written in plain, bleak prose.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a book in the surface, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the ancient classical language of India, still used in Hindu scripture.

clue.text: Hides from king in crowd

indicators.note: the monarch is placed in the middle of the word for a throng

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a mass is a large crowd of people

explanation.surface: A monarch disguising himself among the masses to escape notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To mask something is to conceal or cover it, so masks is a verb matching hides.
